proposed.text: How does the dual-threshold passing requirement (70% weighted average AND no subject below 50%) protect public safety in architectural practice?

options.text: It allows candidates with narrow specialization to become architects, potentially compromising comprehensive skill sets
It prevents candidates with foundational deficiencies in critical areas from practicing
It ensures only wealthy candidates can afford retakes, limiting access to the profession
It simplifies the examination administration process, reducing complexity in scoring

rationale.a: Misrepresents the purpose; the dual threshold actually PREVENTS narrow specialization by requiring competence across all areas.
rationale.c: Conflates examination cost with licensing standards; the dual threshold is a competence measure, not an economic filter.
rationale.d: Ignores public safety; the dual threshold's rigor increases administrative complexity to protect the public, not simplify process.
rationale.correct: The dual-threshold approach prevents candidates from advancing with deficiencies in foundational areas, even if compensated by high performance elsewhere — a critical safeguard for public safety in architectural practice where failures can endanger building occupants.
rationale.takeaway: Dual threshold protects safety: 50% floor prevents licensing candidates with critical foundational gaps, even if strong elsewhere.
